ing: Kefalotyri or Graviera cheese 200g (sliced 1 cm thick)
steps: Dipping: Dip the cheese slice in cold water for 1 minute — this helps the flour adhere better.
Flouring: Lightly flour both sides. Shake off the excess.
Frying: Heat oil in a hot pan (ideally a small saganaki pan). Fry for 1.5-2 minutes per side until golden and just beginning to melt slightly inside. Important: very hot oil gives a crisp exterior.
Serving: Serve immediately in the pan, drizzled with lemon and oregano. Eat while hot.
saganaki.plate: In the pan or on a warm plate with lemon.

steps: Cutting the avocado: Halve the avocado, remove the pit and cut into cubes or slices. Important: drizzle immediately with lemon juice to prevent browning.
Preparation: Halve the cherry tomatoes, cut the cucumber into half-moons, and finely chop the spring onions.
Serving: Toss everything together or arrange on a platter. Drizzle with olive oil and lemon. Season with salt, pepper and fresh herbs. Serve immediately.
salata_avokanto.plate: On a platter with fresh basil.

steps: Make the Caesar dressing: mayonnaise, lemon juice, grated garlic, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Cut the romaine lettuce into pieces and wash thoroughly.
Toss the lettuce with the dressing.
Add the croutons and grated parmesan.
Serve immediately.
Rinse the quinoa and cook according to package instructions (about 15 minutes). Let cool.
Dice the cucumber, cherry tomatoes, avocado, and red onion.
Combine the quinoa with the vegetables and cilantro.
Add the oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately or chilled from the refrigerator.
Hard-boil the eggs (10 minutes), and boil the potatoes and green beans separately.
Slice the tomatoes and cut the eggs into quarters.
Make a dressing with olive oil, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper.
Arrange all the ingredients neatly and separately on the plate.
Drizzle with the dressing and serve.
Boil the beets with their skins on for 45-50 minutes. Peel and cut into small cubes.
Make a dressing with olive oil, balsamic vinegar, honey, salt and pepper.
Spread the arugula on the base of the plate and top with the beets.
Crumble feta on top along with the walnuts and dressing.
Serve immediately.

Preparing the spinach: Wash the 100g baby spinach in cold water and dry it very well, ideally with a salad spinner. Important: the leaves must be completely dry, otherwise the water will dilute the dressing and it won't cling to the leaves.

Cleaning the pomegranate: Cut 1 pomegranate in half and release the seeds by tapping the skin from above with a spoon over a bowl. To avoid staining, do this with the pomegranate submerged in water, where the membrane floats up and the seeds sink.
Toasting the walnuts: Toast the 60g walnuts in a dry skillet (no oil) over medium heat for about 5 minutes, stirring. Toasting releases their oils and intensifies both aroma and crunch.
Dressing: In a bowl, whisk the 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar, 1 tsp honey and 2 tbsp olive oil with a pinch of salt until emulsified and well combined. The honey balances the acidity of the balsamic.
Assembling: On a platter, arrange the spinach, scatter the pomegranate seeds, the toasted walnuts and 80g crumbled feta on top.
Serving: Drizzle with the dressing just before serving and toss gently. Important: add the dressing at the last moment, otherwise the spinach will wilt and lose its freshness.
Spread the arugula on the base of the plate.
Cut the figs into quarters and arrange them over the arugula.
Add slices of prosciutto and chopped walnuts.
Grate parmesan on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic cream, and season with salt and pepper.
Washing: Wash the 100g arugula thoroughly and drain or pat dry with paper towels, so the dressing clings to the leaves and the salad doesn't turn watery.
Cutting the cherry tomatoes: Halve the 100g cherry tomatoes and arrange them with the arugula on a serving platter.
Parmesan: Shave the 60g Parmesan into thin curls with a vegetable peeler. Important: never grated, as thin shavings give a better texture and a more pronounced presence of flavor in every bite.
Dressing: Drizzle the salad with the 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar and the 2 tbsp olive oil, so the acidity balances with the oil.
Serving: Grind fresh pepper on top and serve immediately, as arugula wilts quickly once the dressing is added.
salata_rokka.plate: Parmesan shaved into curls — that's what makes the difference!

ing: Mayonnaise 3 tbsp or olive oil 4 tbsp
steps: Draining the tuna: Drain the tuna well and flake it with a fork into large pieces. Important: draining matters — the tin oil is neutral and would dilute the dressing.
Boiling the eggs: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes for a firm but not chalky yolk, then cool them at once in iced water so they peel cleanly.
Taming the onion: Slice the red onion thinly and soak it in cold water with a little lemon for 10 minutes, to take the harsh bite out of it.
Preparing the greens: Wash the lettuce, dry it thoroughly and tear it by hand into bite-sized pieces. Wet leaves repel the dressing.
Making the dressing: Whisk the mayonnaise or oil with the lemon juice, chopped dill, salt and pepper into a smooth emulsion.
Assembling: Layer the lettuce in a wide bowl, then the tuna, the corn, the halved cherry tomatoes, the drained onion and the capers.
Adding the eggs: Cut the eggs into quarters and arrange them around the edge instead of mixing them in, so they stay whole and presentable.
Dressing: Pour the dressing over only at the moment of serving. Dressed early, the lettuce wilts within minutes.
salata_tonou.wine: A dry white Sauvignon Blanc or a Greek Assyrtiko.
salata_tonou.plate: Serve in a wide shallow bowl with the egg quarters around the rim and dill scattered over the top.

steps: Boiling the pasta: Cook the pasta in well-salted water until just al dente — it firms up further as it cools, so do not overcook it.
Cooling: Important: Drain and rinse it under cold water to stop the cooking, then toss it with a spoonful of oil so it does not clump into a block.
Chopping the vegetables: Cut the cucumber and pepper into small even dice and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Draining the tomatoes: Let the halved tomatoes sit in a sieve with a pinch of salt for 10 minutes, so their juice does not water down the salad later.
Making the dressing: Whisk the oil, vinegar, oregano, salt and pepper until emulsified and slightly thickened.
Combining: Toss the cooled pasta with the vegetables, the olives and half the dressing, and mix gently.
Chilling: Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Pasta salad needs this time — the pasta absorbs the dressing and the flavours settle together.
Finishing: Just before serving, add the crumbled feta, the fresh basil and the rest of the dressing, and check the seasoning — cold food always needs more salt than it seems.
salata_zymarikon.wine: A chilled rosé or a light white Roditis.
salata_zymarikon.plate: Serve in a wide bowl at cool room temperature, with feta crumbled over the top and basil leaves.

steps: Purging the snails: Important: Keep the live snails for 5-7 days in a covered ventilated container with flour or bran, so they empty themselves. This step is not optional for safety.
Washing: Wash them repeatedly in plenty of water with a little vinegar, until the water runs completely clear.
Blanching: Boil them for 5 minutes in salted water, then drain them well.
Drying: Dry them very well and dry the shell openings too. Important: any water left inside will spit violently the moment it hits the hot oil.
Coating with flour: Dip the open face of each snail in flour, tapping off the excess. The flour seals the opening and forms the crust.
Heating the oil: Heat the oil in a wide pan until it is very hot — this dish only works at high heat.
Frying: Place the snails opening-side down into the oil — this is what boubouristi means — and fry them for 2-3 minutes without moving them.
Adding the vinegar: Stand back and pour in the vinegar. It will spit and steam violently. Let it evaporate for 1-2 minutes.
Finishing: Add the rosemary and coarse salt, swirl the pan once and serve immediately while sizzling.
saligkaria_boubouristi.wine: Cretan raki or a robust white wine with acidity.
saligkaria_boubouristi.plate: Serve straight from the pan, opening-side up, with the vinegar sauce and bread to mop it up.

steps: Melting the butter: Melt the 60g butter in a small saucepan over low heat, so it doesn't burn and turn bitter.
Sautéing the garlic: Add 3 cloves of chopped garlic and sauté for 1-2 minutes, just until fragrant. Important: don't let it brown, as burnt garlic turns bitter and ruins the sauce.
Adding the lemon: Add the 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp zest, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, and thyme or oregano. The zest adds intense aroma without extra acidity.
Thickening the sauce: Stir and simmer for 2-3 minutes until it thickens slightly and the flavors come together. The mustard helps emulsify the sauce.
Seasoning: Taste and add salt and pepper as needed, keeping the lemon's acidity in mind.
Finishing and serving: Remove from the heat, add chopped parsley, and pour immediately over the hot chicken. Important: serve it hot, since the heat releases the aromas and brings the dish to life.
saltsa_kotopoulo.wine: Dry white or a light rosé.
saltsa_kotopoulo.plate: Pour over fillet or thigh, garnish with lemon peel and thyme.

steps: Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, oregano, salt and pepper.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in fresh basil at the end.
Use for pasta, pizza, or as a base for other recipes.

ing: Syrup: Sugar 250g, Water 250ml, Orange blossom water 2 tbsp
steps: Syrup: Boil the sugar, water, and orange blossom water for 5 minutes. Let cool.
Batter: Combine the semolina, coconut, sugar, yogurt, eggs, melted butter, and baking powder.
Baking: Spread the batter evenly in a greased pan. Sprinkle almonds on top. Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes.
Scoring: As soon as it comes out of the oven, score into diamonds or squares.
Soaking: Pour the cold syrup over it immediately. Let it absorb completely — at least 30 minutes. Important: cold syrup on a hot cake ensures perfect absorption without becoming overly soggy.
samali.plate: Cut into diamonds with almonds on top.

steps: Cleaning: Clean the 500g fresh sardines, removing the innards and, if you like, the heads, and rinse very well under cold water. Important: dry them very thoroughly with paper towels, since moisture prevents browning and causes the oil to spatter in the pan.
Salting: Salt the sardines just before cooking. Salting too early draws out their moisture and dries them out.
Flouring (optional): For a crispier crust, dust them lightly with flour and shake off the excess, so they don't pick up too much flour and become heavy.
Cooking: Cook on a hot grill or in a pan with 3 tbsp olive oil for 3-4 minutes per side, until browned and the flesh turns opaque. Avoid turning them repeatedly so they don't fall apart.
Lemon-oil dressing: Mix the juice of 2 lemons with a little olive oil and oregano for a fresh dressing that cuts through the fish's richness.
Serving: Serve immediately while hot, drizzled with the lemon-oil dressing, oregano and coarse salt.
sardeles_lemonates.plate: With lemon, olives and fresh bread. The essence of Greek summer.

steps: Beat the yolks with the sugar over a bain-marie for about 8 minutes, until pale, thick and warm to the touch.
Important: The bowl must never touch the water and the heat must stay low, or the yolks scramble and the mixture is ruined.
Take it off the heat and keep beating until it has cooled completely to room temperature.
Whip the cream separately to soft peaks — softer than for a cake, because it stiffens further in the freezer.
Fold the cream into the cooled yolk mixture in three additions, gently, keeping as much air as possible.
Fold in the chopped hazelnuts and grated chocolate.
Line a loaf tin with cling film, leaving a generous overhang, and pour in the mixture.
Freeze for at least 6 hours. Unlike ice cream, semifreddo needs no churning — the whipped air is what keeps it soft.
Turn it out using the cling film and slice while still frozen, then let the slices stand for 5 minutes before serving.
semifredo.plate: Cut into slices and serve with toasted hazelnuts and chocolate sauce.

steps: Wash the chard well and cut the stems into pieces.
Bring salted water to a boil.
Boil the stems first for 5 minutes, then add the leaves for another 5-8 minutes.
Drain well.
Serve warm with a generous drizzle of olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Cut the puff pastry into squares.
Place feta on each square and season with pepper.
Fold into a triangle and press the edges to seal.
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Boiling the potatoes: Boil the 4 large potatoes whole, skin-on, in salted water until tender. The skin keeps the potatoes from absorbing too much water and becoming watery.
Peeling: Peel the potatoes while still hot. Important: hot potato mashes evenly and binds better with the oil, while cold potato becomes gluey.
Crushing the garlic: Crush the 6-8 garlic cloves with a little salt in a mortar until it becomes a paste. The salt helps grind the garlic and releases its aromatics.
Combining: Add the hot potatoes and mash them together with the garlic in the mortar, or briefly in a blender, until you have a smooth base.
Emulsifying: Add the 150ml olive oil and the 2 tbsp vinegar alternately, in small amounts, beating continuously until the skordalia becomes creamy and fluffy.
Finishing: Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar. Important: don't overwork the potato in the blender, as it releases starch and turns gluey like paste.
skordalia.plate: Bowl, olive oil, olives. With salt cod.

steps: Flattening the meat: Place each slice between two sheets of cling film and beat it with a mallet or rolling pin to an even 5 mm thickness. Important: even thickness is everything — thin edges burn while thick centres stay raw.
Seasoning: Season both sides with salt and pepper and let the slices sit for 10 minutes.
Setting up the coating: Line up three shallow dishes: flour, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs.
Coating: Dip each slice in flour and shake off the excess, then in egg letting the surplus drip away, then press it firmly into the breadcrumbs.
Resting the coating: Let the coated schnitzels rest for 10 minutes. This lets the crumb bind to the egg, so the crust does not slide off in the pan.
Heating the oil: Heat plenty of oil to 175°C in a wide pan — a crumb dropped in should sizzle immediately without browning instantly.
Frying: Fry for 3-4 minutes per side until deep golden, turning only once. Turning repeatedly breaks the crust.
Not crowding: Fry two at a time at most. Important: a crowded pan drops the oil temperature and the coating soaks up fat instead of crisping.
Draining: Drain on a rack, not on paper — paper traps steam underneath and the bottom crust goes soft.
Serving: Serve immediately with lemon wedges.
snitsel_xoirino.wine: A cold beer, or a crisp white such as Moschofilero.
snitsel_xoirino.plate: Serve one schnitzel per plate covering most of it, with a lemon half and fries or mashed potato on the side.

ing: Veal, top round or shoulder, sliced 800g
steps: Preparation: Lightly pound the veal slices to tenderize them and season with salt and pepper. Dust with flour on both sides, shaking off the excess.
Searing: Heat the olive oil well in a deep skillet and sear the slices over high heat until nicely browned on both sides. Transfer to a pot.
The secret of the sauce: In the same oil, add the chopped garlic and parsley and sauté for half a minute, just until fragrant, without letting them burn.
Deglazing: Deglaze with the vinegar and wine, let the alcohol evaporate for 1-2 minutes, and pour the sauce over the meat.
Important: authentic Sofrito contains no tomato. Its characteristic white color and tangy flavor come solely from the vinegar, garlic, and parsley, so don't be tempted to add tomato paste.
Simmering: Add a little hot water so the meat is almost covered, cover with the lid, and simmer over low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours.
Thickening: The meat is ready when it becomes very tender and the sauce reduces to a velvety consistency. If needed, uncover toward the end to let the sauce thicken.
Serving: Taste for salt and serve hot, spooning the sauce generously over the top.
sofrito.wine: Dry white wine, ideally a Corfiot Kakotrygis.
sofrito.plate: Serve with mashed potatoes or fluffy rice to soak up the white sauce.

ing: Sugar 1.5 cups with 2 tbsp cocoa (for the syrup)
steps: Preparation: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan and butter or line with parchment paper a baking pan about 25x35 cm.
Mixing the dry ingredients: In a large bowl, sift together the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and add the sugar, mixing well.
Mixing the wet ingredients: In a second bowl, whisk the eggs with the oil, milk and vanilla until smooth.

Combining: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and whisk until the batter is smooth. Important: Don't overmix the batter, as this develops the gluten and the cake turns out dense and chewy instead of light.
Baking: Pour the mixture into the pan and bake for 30-35 minutes, until risen and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Syrup: While it bakes, boil the water with the sugar and cocoa in a saucepan for 4-5 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Syruping: As soon as the cake comes out, score it into pieces and slowly pour the hot syrup over the hot cake so it soaks in evenly.
Resting: Let the chocolate cake cool and absorb the syrup for at least 2 hours before serving.
sokolatopita.wine: Sweet Mavrodafni wine or a hot coffee.
sokolatopita.plate: Serve in pieces with a scoop of vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.

steps: Marinade: Mix the olive oil, juice of half a lemon, thinly sliced garlic, salt, pepper and dill. For a sweet-and-sour touch, add honey and soy sauce. Coat the fillets and let rest for 15 minutes.

Baking: Place the fillets on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes, depending on thickness. Important: the salmon is done when it flakes easily with a fork and the center is still slightly pink.
Serving: Serve immediately with lemon slices, fresh dill, and rice or roasted vegetables on the side.
solomos_fournou.plate: With lemon slices and fresh dill.
